modules.module_title: Preparing for programming CNC machine for production

pcs.pc_description: obtain job specification from a valid and approved source
read and establish job requirements from the job specification document accurately
follow job instructions, assembly drawings and laid down procedures at all times
report and rectify incorrect and inconsistent information in job specification documents as per organization procedures
use and extract information from reference charts, tables, graphs and standards
prepare the work area as per procedure or operational specification
conduct a preliminary check of the readiness of the program so that the CNC machine operates correctly
determine what operational objectives and targets need to be achieved and how best the machine needs to be programmed to achieve this
extract and use information from engineering drawings and related specifications in relation to work undertaken
identify tool requirements from tooling layout and assess their suitability
identify suitable work holding or fixturing device as per the job requirement
ensure the correct and latest part-program is uploaded onto the CNC system
• Use Electric Discharge Machining to hole out blind spots and also to create • hole in the die formation plate/ work piece
• Setup the electrodes of the EDM machine and measure the distance between • the electrodes as mentioned in the Work Instructions
Ensure that the correct current and voltage are selected for the EDM process
• Ensure that the work piece/ metal piece is carefully loaded on the EDM • machine surface tables/ work platform using manual/ automatic tools
• Ensure that there is uniform flow of dielectric liquid i.e. flushing of the • dielectric liquid to remove any debris which would have collected during the • EDM process
• Ensure that the machine operations are regularly monitored to detect any • malfunctions in machine operations or any out of tolerance machining
• Ensure that the electrode properties like surface, dimensions, metallurgical • properties are periodically checked as per the checklist provided
• Ensure that the electrodes are changed in case there is a deviation from the • specifications

modules.module_title: Carrying out programming for CNC machine

pcs.pc_description: Prepare the CNC program with commands for tool motions, spindle motions, miscellaneous functions and tool change, in syntax corresponding to the machine and control system on which the component will be machined
various ways to make CNC program are by writing it on paper or in a computer's text editor, or using CAM software or controllers on machine
ensure that the part program is efficient and results in minimal cycle time, with optimal cutting parameters and no unnecessary tool motions
use subprograms and canned cycles, to reduce program size and input time and avoid memory overflow on the machine
transfer the program to the machine by entering it at the console or transmitting it through a wired link or through a data transfer device
follow the correct procedures for calling up the program and dealing with any error messages or faults
handle the typical problems that can occur with the programming, loading and editing activities effectively using approved procedures
save the proven program in the appropriate storage medium – paper, computer hard disk, etc. - and location
complete relevant documentation as per procedure
leave the work area in a safe and tidy condition on completion of the activities

modules.module_title: Test and prove the program on the CNC Machine

pcs.pc_description: obtain appropriate equipment or tools needed as per job requirements
ensure that all measuring equipment is calibrated and approved for usage
ensure that the tools and fixtures are in usable condition(eg. free from breakage, damage, calibration, etc.)
pre-set the tooling appropriately using setting jigs/fixtures
seek any necessary instruction/training on the operation of the machine where required
mount tools in the correct positions in the tool turret or magazine
check that the tools have been mounted in positions corresponding to tool numbers in the part program
measure tool and work offset data - X and Z offsets for lathes; work offsets, length offsets and tool radius for machining centers
ensure that the component is free of burrs, chips or other material adhering to its butting surfaces
mount the part on machine firmly in the specified work holding devices, with the appropriate clamping forces
enter work offset and tool data on the machine – X and Z offsets, tool orientation and Nose radius for lathes; length offsets and tool radius for machining centers
ensure that tool data has been entered in offset number corresponding to the tool offset numbers in the part program
deal with error messages and faults on the program or equipment
• cut a trial part using single block run, dry run and feed and speed override • controls
edit the program and adjust tool and wear offsets to correct any dimensional errors on the part
ensure that the trial part conforms to drawing specifications in terms of dimensions, surface finishes and geometrical parameters like concentricity, parallelism, run out, etc.
hand-over the machine to the machine operator for machining the batch of parts, along with relevant instructions and documentation on periodic inspection of components, change of worn out tools
correct the tool wear offsets whenever required, based on the results of the period inspection
change worn out tools and indexable inserts whenever required
after every change of a worn out tool or insert, cut a trial part and correct any dimensional inaccuracies by adjusting the tool offsets or wear offsets
return worn out cutting tools, work holding device / fixtures / instruments / drawings to store
ensure that there is no damage to the tool/fixture while doing the prove-out
shut down the equipment to a safe condition on conclusion of the activities
deal promptly and effectively with problems within span of responsibility and control and report those that cannot be solved
